Ready. **Open → http://maker:4001/edge-dup.html** (it starts with three bookmarks; one, "Flask", is in the **Finished** tab).

**1. Saving a link you already have.**
- Expand **"＋ Save a link"** and paste `https://github.com/pallets/flask` (the Flask one that's already saved, in Finished). Click **Save bookmark**.
- Instead of adding a copy, it shows a blue note *"You've already saved this — here it is…"*, switches to the **Finished** tab where that bookmark lives, **highlights it** with a brief flash, and opens it ready to edit.

**2. Editing the existing bookmark right there.**
- In that opened editor, type `revisit` in the Tags box and press **Enter** to add it as a chip, then click **Save changes**. The bookmark updates in place (and flashes again).
- You can also use the **✓ Finished / ↩ To read** button to change its status.

**3. Editing any bookmark anytime.**
- On a different bookmark, click its **Edit** button — you can change the title, description, and tags the same way, then Save changes or Cancel.

A couple of things I decided that I'd like your judgement on:
- I treat two links as **"the same"** when the web address matches ignoring a trailing "/" and upper/lower case (so `github.com/pallets/flask` and `GitHub.com/pallets/flask/` count as duplicates). Reasonable, or too loose/strict?
- **Editing** covers the **title, description, tags, and read-status** — is that the full set of things you'd want to change about a saved bookmark, or is anything missing?
